audit.why: Emerald+ headline for Ambessa into Gragas top is 53.03% over 264 games. One number, no tier split.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Gragas four stages (L2, L3, first item, two items) and Ambessa zero, while the prose says 'At 3 it tips your way', 'First item is your peak' and 'in the 1v1 you own him all game'. A 53% matchup whose chart never once names the owner is self-contradicting.
audit.why: Ambessa's whole kit (Cunning Sweep -> Sundering Slam, Lacerate, the Drakehound's Step dash) is online at 3, and Gragas has one 14s escape to answer a repeatable dash chain. Gragas is an AP bruiser with no scaling kite pattern, so he does not reclaim the duel at two items.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Gragas / Ambessa / Gragas / Ambessa / Ambessa / Ambessa in both layers. Difficulty is early-weighted: he owns levels 1-5 through Drunken Rage's permanent damage cut, you own 6 onward.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text leaned on 'R passive armor-pen' and 'on-ability healing' for Ambessa. Neither appears anywhere in Riot's text for Drakehound's Step or Public Execution.
audit.why: Riot's Public Execution description is blink-to-farthest-champion, suppress, slam for damage and a stun — no penetration and no healing. Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund. The kit file's 'heal' flag on R contradicts Riot's own description and is a tooltip-parse misfire.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten around verified numbers: level 3 (full kit, Body Slam is 14s at rank 1), level 6 (1250-unit blink + suppress + stun on a 130s cooldown), first item (Eclipse/Profane plus rank-5 Q at 10s), and Gragas's own level 2-3 swing off a 5s Drunken Rage.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated. Repudiation (W) is written as generic 'shielding' and Body Slam is called an 'escape' without ever noting that it stuns. Nothing keyed either kit's cooldowns to the other's.
audit.why: Repudiation deals increased damage if it blocks any non-minion damage while bracing — Barrel Roll's blast is the safe thing to brace, because Body Slam stuns and a stun landing in the brace window is unverified behaviour. Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s and is simultaneously his engage, his stun and his only disengage from a Lacerate slow; Barrel Roll is 850 range against your 650 Q, so he wins every exchange you start at his range. Public Execution's suppression is the answer to the escape half.
audit.corrected: Stated across early/mid/wants: brace Repudiation on Barrel Roll for the bonus damage, not on the wave; treat Body Slam's 14s as the all-in timer; use Public Execution's suppress specifically against the Body Slam disengage; Explosive Cask on 100/85/70s is his one tool that displaces you mid-dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: Trading advice said 'Drunken Rage damage-reduced Body Slam' without the cooldown, so it read as an occasional threat.
audit.why: Drunken Rage is a flat 5s cooldown for 30 mana. His damage reduction is effectively permanent in lane; it is not a window you can wait out, which is why the early trade maths favour him and why you trade off Body Slam instead.
audit.corrected: Both spikes[3].text and whys[3] now name the 5s cooldown and redirect the trade trigger to a spent Body Slam.

audit.why: Body Slam was already the named cooldown to track; the numbers are now attached to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds even though Happy Hour heals Gragas on every skill cast.
audit.why: Happy Hour is a periodic heal off ability use — it is exactly the sustain that turns your won short trades back into even ones over a lane. The full layer's itemization line already calls anti-heal core, so the two layers disagreed.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal now named in wants.you[2], whys[5], spikes[2].text and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Critical Don'ts said 'Fight in his Q puddle'. Barrel Roll is a cask that detonates on command or after 4 seconds; there is no lingering puddle.
audit.why: The real mistake is letting the cask sit — its potency increases the longer it waits before it blows.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to 'Let his cask ripen under you' with the 4-second detonation.

audit.whatIsWrong: Public Execution's targeting quirk was never explained — text says it 'blinks you behind him' with no range or targeting rule.
audit.why: It blinks to the FARTHEST enemy champion in the line you aim, up to 1250 units. In a 1v1 that reads as a long gap-close, but with his jungler nearby it will take the far champion instead of Gragas.
audit.corrected: Range and blink behaviour stated in spikes[1].text, whys[4], wants.you[1] and mid.

edits.before: Levels 1 and 2 this is even — you have one ability and long cooldowns, while Gragas can pop Drunken Rage and Body Slam into a Barrel Roll for a chunky trade you can't yet answer. Don't walk up to throw a single Q he can just Body-Slam through. At 3 it tips your way: land Q's cone to unlock Sundering Slam, then E-spin for the near-total slow and Drakehound-dash to stay glued to him — that's the window his Body Slam can't disengage out of. Respect his E baiting you under tower; let him commit it first, then punish the cooldown.
edits.after: Levels 1 and 2 are even — one ability and long cooldowns, while Drunken Rage's 5s cooldown hands him a permanent damage cut into a Body Slam stun you can't yet answer. Don't throw a lone Cunning Sweep he can Body-Slam through. At 3 it tips your way: land the Q cone to arm Sundering Slam, then Lacerate for the slow and Drakehound-dash to stay glued — Body Slam is 14s at rank 1, so it disengages once and no more. Brace Repudiation on his Barrel Roll, not the wave: non-minion damage blocked makes its slam hit harder.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your soft spot — your cooldowns are longest here and a Drunken-Rage-empowered Gragas can out-brawl you, so farm and don't force extended fights without your combo up. At 6 you flip it: Public Execution blinks you behind him, suppresses through his Body Slam escape and stuns, and your R passive armor-pen plus on-ability healing turn the brawl in your favor. Bait the Body Slam, dash in on its cooldown, and chain Q1-auto-Q2 with E to lock him. Watch his Explosive Cask — he'll save it to peel your dash or to flip you back into his tower.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your soft spot — your Q still sits on 13-11s while Drunken Rage refreshes every 5s, so farm and don't force extended fights without your combo up. At 6 you flip it: Public Execution blinks up to 1250 units to him, suppresses him straight through the Body Slam escape, then slams him down stunned — more lockdown than a 14s dash can trade with. Bait the Body Slam, dash in on its cooldown, and chain Q1-auto-Q2 with Lacerate. Watch Explosive Cask — on 100s he saves it to knock your dash away or flip you into his tower.

edits.before: First item is your peak — Eclipse or Profane plus the level 9 Q max means Q1-auto-Q2 halves his health while your shielding and on-ability healing keep you full, and you beat him in a straight brawl. Unlike a hard-scaling carry, Gragas doesn't reclaim this lane at two items: he's an AP bruiser, not a kiter, so your R gap-close, armor-pen and ability-weaving stay ahead of his item sustain and displacement. Keep forcing the all-in on his Body Slam and Cask cooldowns. The only thing to fear late is his teamfight Explosive Cask catching you mid-dash — in the 1v1 you own him all game.
edits.after: First item is your peak — Eclipse or Profane plus the level 9 Q max drops the Q to 10s, so Q1-auto-Q2 halves his health while Repudiation's shield eats the return, and you beat him in a straight brawl. Unlike a hard-scaling carry, Gragas doesn't reclaim this lane at two items: he's an AP bruiser, not a kiter, so your R gap-close and ability-weaving stay ahead of him. Keep Grievous Wounds up — Happy Hour heals him off every cast, and that trickle is what drags your won trades back to even. The one late threat is a teamfight Explosive Cask catching you mid-dash.

edits.after: Cunning Sweep into Sundering Slam, Lacerate's slow and the Drakehound dash all land inside Body Slam's 14s — take the short trade on it.

notes: Two data-quality issues found in champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json: the derived flags put 'grounding' on Repudiation (W) and 'grounding' plus 'heal' on Public Execution (R). Riot's own descriptions contain neither — the parser almost certainly fired on the words 'slams the ground' and 'into the ground'. I treated Ambessa as having no grounding and no ultimate healing. Separately, the Ambessa content layer repeatedly asserts an 'R passive armor-pen' and 'on-ability healing' for Ambessa across many matchups; neither is in Riot's text for any of her five abilities. I removed those claims from the strings I rewrote here rather than restating them, but they remain in the other ~65 Ambessa matchups and should be swept. The packet's levelChart for this matchup does not match either layer on disk (packet says Skill/Skill/Ambessa/Skill/Ambessa/Ambessa/Ambessa; disk said Skill/Gragas/Gragas/Skill/Skill/Gragas/Gragas) — I worked from disk, which is what the applier compares against.
